note: Seed variant lanes. A lane is a named library set a prompt can be pinned to. Vanilla is a lane like any other, not 'the original' — the baseline has to be a cell in the grid to be comparable.

lanes.label: Vanilla Canvas
lanes.note: No provisioned library. The control cell — everything is hand-written against the raw canvas and Web Audio APIs.

lanes.label: p5.js
lanes.note: Creative-coding loop. Global mode setup()/draw(); approachable 2D.

lanes.label: Phaser
lanes.note: Full 2D engine — scenes, input, sprites, tilemaps and Arcade physics come for free.

lanes.label: PixiJS
lanes.note: Renderer only. The loop, input and game rules stay project code.

lanes.label: KAPLAY
lanes.note: Terse arcade-flavoured 2D engine with a component/tag scene model.

lanes.label: Kontra.js
lanes.note: Tiny 2D toolkit. Little is supplied, so most of the game is written by hand.

lanes.label: melonJS
lanes.note: Classic tile-and-entity 2D engine with a built-in game loop and state stack.

lanes.label: Three.js 3D
lanes.note: r128 core only — no OrbitControls, GLTFLoader or examples/jsm add-ons.

lanes.label: Babylon.js 3D
lanes.note: Batteries-included 3D engine with its own scene graph, cameras and materials.

lanes.label: PlayCanvas 3D
lanes.note: Entity/component 3D engine driven from code rather than its editor.

lanes.label: Phaser + Howler
lanes.note: 2D engine with an explicit audio layer, so sound is a first-class requirement.

lanes.label: p5.js + Tone
lanes.note: Creative coding with synthesis — for games where audio is part of the mechanic.

lanes.label: Three.js + Rapier 3D
lanes.note: 3D rendering with real rigid-body physics rather than hand-rolled motion.
